vulnerability.title: Ensure PAM Enforces Password Requirements - Prevent the Use of Dictionary Words
vulnerability.description: The pam_pwquality module's dictcheck check if passwords contains dictionary words. When dictcheck is set to 1 passwords will be checked for dictionary words.
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q kernel-core && { rpm --quiet -q libpwquality; }; then var_password_pam_dictcheck='' if grep -sq dictcheck /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf ; then sed -i "/dictcheck/d" /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf fi # Strip any search characters in the key arg so that the key can be replaced without # adding any search characters to the config file. stripped_key=$(sed 's/[\^=\$,;+]*//g' <<< "^dictcheck") # shellcheck disable=SC2059 printf -v formatted_output "%s = %s" "$stripped_key" "$var_password_pam_dictcheck" # If the key exists, change it. Otherwise, add it to the config_file. # We search for the key string followed by a word boundary (matched by \>), # so if we search for 'setting', 'setting2' won't match. if LC_AL

triage_decision.reason: The remediation involves editing a PAM configuration file to enable dictionary word checking, a standard STIG hardening step that does not affect critical services or system boot. It is unlikely to lock out users or break the system.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: authentication/authorization affected; Potential user lockout if passwords contain dictionary words

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan correctly targets the dictionary-check requirement and will enforce `dictcheck = 1`. It preserves existing content and uses in-place editing, which is safe and reversible. However, it only touches the base config file and may miss overrides in `-d/*.conf` directories. The regex used in `sed` could fail on lines with leading whitespace, inline comments or multiple entries. Adding a backup step and scanning all relevant files would make the fix more robust.
concerns: May not account for overrides in /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf
sed pattern may not match lines with leading whitespace or comments
suggested_improvements: Add a backup command before modifying the file
Use a more robust regex to match dictcheck lines, handling whitespace and comments
Validate the new setting with `pamtester` or similar after change
